target_capability: persistent prefix and exact backend-frontier recovery
assertions: The response separates rendered-byte-prefix lookup from validated exact-token/model-state payload restoration.
It preserves saved exact tokens and tokenizes only the suffix after the byte prefix, rather than retokenizing the whole prefix into the old backend state.
It checks model identity, saved context not exceeding current context, optional same-quant policy, and payload version/layout constraints without claiming arbitrary checkpoint compatibility.
It rejects token-vector-only rewrites behind the live end and calls for verified older-frontier restoration or full replay.
It explains that all calls in a message must resolve to one retained DSML block, missing/mixed mappings use canonical fallback, and tool IDs alone are not durable conversation storage.
It states that TP payload reload rebuilds both ranks from exact saved tokens and still needs real distributed-backend verification.
It neither starts a service nor deletes or patches cache data, and distinguishes the proposed recovery from an executed result.
